rows.description: I discover my partner took credit, funds, or a deal behind my back and feel shock and rage. I secure records, seek legal and trusted advice, and confront calmly; public smearing or revenge usually harms me too.

rows.description: I cut a corner or hid a decision from my co-founder and now feel uneasy. I come clean early, offer repair, and restore agreements; excuses like it was for the company's good will not rebuild trust.

rows.description: My co-founder gets the media credit and investor attention and I feel invisible and bitter. I say it to them directly, agree on fair credit and roles, and avoid quietly undermining them.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, betrayal, disillusionment, exploitation, forgiveness, grief

rows.description: I place complete trust in my co-founder and skip contracts because we are friends. Warm trust is a strength, but clear written roles, equity, and exit terms protect the friendship as well as the business.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, betrayal, disillusionment, envy, exploitation, forgiveness

rows.description: My partner and I argue about direction, pace, and money and it turns personal. We separate the idea from the person, set decision rules, and use an outside advisor when stuck; contempt is the sign to stop and repair.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: betrayal, disillusionment, envy, exploitation, forgiveness, grief

rows.description: My partner stayed loyal through a rough patch and I feel deeply grateful. I show it with fair equity, recognition, and honest updates, and avoid treating loyalty as something that will always be there without care.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, betrayal, disillusionment, envy, exploitation, forgiveness

rows.description: My partner keeps making me carry more work for less credit or pay and I feel used but afraid to lose the venture. I state the imbalance, propose a written fix, and prepare to walk away if nothing changes.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, betrayal, disillusionment, envy, forgiveness, grief

rows.description: Beyond anger, the loss of partnership and shared dream brings grief. Allow yourself to mourn, get legal advice on separation, and avoid mixing the emotional and financial talks. Healing helps you choose better next time.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: argument, betrayal, disillusionment, envy, exploitation, forgiveness

rows.description: You realise you wronged your partner and they are hurt. Own it clearly, offer restitution, and accept consequences without demanding forgiveness. Justifying yourself with they did it too keeps the injury alive.

rows.description: I have just become manager over former peers and fear they think I don't deserve it. I am honest about what I don't know, listen more than I prove myself, and let results build authority rather than acting bossy.
